Summary

"And?" He asks tiredly, manages to make a circle in the air with his hand before it flops back down to the ground uselessly. "I'm willing to bet anything that I've loved you since our first real meeting, even if I cannot recall it."

Mydei considers him carefully for a long moment. An unreadable look crosses his face before he shakes it off. "You are hopeless," he says quietly.

Phainon smiles, a smaller but no less genuine expression. Mydei's gaze snaps to his lips, and Phainon revels in the knowledge that his eyes haven't left him once, even after their battle ended. He hums happily. "Perhaps so."

or; Phainon loses his memory, and is convinced he is dating Mydei. Upon finding out he isn't, he makes attempts at courting.

His breath hitches at the piercing pain striking through his skull. He resists the urge to reach up and press his hand against the spot at the back of his head in an attempt to quell it, but just barely so.

"Oh," someone breathes out near him. A shuffling noise as they get closer. "He is waking up."

It's a soft voice, feminine and dripping with concern. He feels the urge to assure her he's alright, and ignore the dizzying headache. Opening his mouth is as far as he gets, wincing when the pain only intensifies.

"Easy," another voice mumbles, deep and regal despite it being just one word. He exhales slowly, and some anxiety he didn't know he felt leaves him. "Don't strain yourself, Deliverer."

The man sounds somewhat amused, and he feels the burning need to say something back, make a comment that will get him a scoff. A muscle memory, perhaps. Before he can make another attempt, bright light shines through his closed eyelids. It's pleasant, familiar. A relaxing sensation that has his body slackening into the soft bed he is lying on. Gradually, the headache eases until it's nothing more than a dull throb. Effortless to ignore as he intended to.

His eyes open, blinking against the vibrant colors.

A short girl stands at his side, one hand retreating from where it rested against his forehead. She's got pink hair tied into twin tails, adorned with fluffy ties. Cyan eyes that are busy scanning his face for any adverse reaction. White and burgundy clothes, almost like a uniform. She is the one taking care of him.

He sends her a genuine smile, hoping to erase the worry in her features just like she got rid of his pain. "Thank you," he rasps out, clearing his throat when his voice cracks from how dry it feels.

Immediately, a glass is pressed against his lips. It comes from the other side of his bed, and he gratefully takes a long sip before glancing over at the person responsible. He inhales too fast once his eyes fall on the man, and he chokes on the water.

Pretty, pretty, pretty.

Messy blond hair that fades into red, sharp molten gold eyes, red marks a stark contrast to the pale skin. And half his chest is exposed for all to see.

That's as far as he gets with taking in all the details, as his lungs force him into a desperate attempt at getting rid of the water that went in the wrong direction. He curls in on himself, coughing and gasping for air. Fuck. Talk about a bad first impression.

"Lord Phainon!" The girl yelps, rushing closer to keep him upright.

Phainon. There it is. He nods to himself, the name fitting perfectly.

Her palm presses against his back, and the pressure to cough up his lungs decreases, leaving only a sore feeling. She frets, rubbing her hand in a soothing motion once it becomes clear he's not in danger of suffocating due to a sip of water. Embarrassing.

"Do you have a death wish?" The man scolds him once Phainon has himself back under control. He doesn't appear concerned about the potential choking, though, glaring as his eyes dart to some spot on Phainon's head. "Taking a blow meant for me when I am immortal, what were you thinking?

Oh. Okay.

Two new pieces of information.

The gorgeous man is immortal. It's reassuring, somehow. That this not-stranger wouldn't die no matter what. It must also mean he's truly important to Phainon. He risked his life to spare this man unnecessary pain despite the fact that an injury wouldn't truly endanger him.

Which brings him to the other fact. Namely, that Phainon was in a fight. It makes sense, he thinks. He knows deep down he is skilled in combat. Enjoys it, even. He didn't realize until it got brought to his attention that he may have participated in it.

"Lord Mydei," the lady admonishes quietly. "Let him rest before you start an argument. You two have a habit of escalating them into fights, and it won't do you any good."

The man, Mydei, rolls his eyes with disdain. "Please. Perhaps it would be beneficial for him to get that brain of his rattled around, finally find some sense somewhere in that skull."

"Don't act like you weren't worried," she tells him, hands resting against her hips and gaze stern. "You remained at his bedside for—"

"Yes," he interrupts her forcefully. His jaw twitches, and he crosses his arms. "You've made your point."

Phainon's eyes get a little stuck on those crossed arms. Red tattoos snake around them, almost artfully. The otherwise pale shade of his skin turns slightly darker above Mydei's elbows, but Phainon is a little preoccupied taking in the way his muscles bulge obscenely. Titans above, it should be illegal to walk shirtless with a physique of this sort. How is anyone supposed to focus?

He shakes his head, trying his best to dispel those thoughts.

He doesn't know Mydei. But his heart beats a little faster when he hears his voice or stares at him. His anxiety fades under his attention. It cannot be a simple reaction to someone attractive. And Mydei himself, he apparently spent time sitting at Phainon's side and waited for him to wake up.

Who is this man to him?

"Sorry," Phainon offers Mydei sheepishly, not flinching despite the vicious glare thrown his way. "I don't think I remember that." It's silent for a moment, but no one seems overly concerned. Right, he injured his head. He supposes it would make sense not to remember the accident itself. He hates to cause more alarm than necessary in his companions, but he needs more information about what's going on. So, he amends, "I don't remember much at all, actually."

One more beat, and the healer lady makes a concerned noise, grabbing a nearby clipboard to jot something down. Mydei frowns; his brows furrow together, and his lips press into a thin line. Phainon finds himself smiling at him helplessly. He doesn't like making people worry. But especially not this man, for some reason. He shouldn't be concerned about Phainon.

"Do you recall your name?" She asks, biting her lip.

"Um, Phainon." He scratches the back of his head, fingers catching on a bandage. Mydei slaps Phainon's hand away, the action followed by an annoyed click of a tongue. He ignores him. "But only because you called me that already."

She sighs a little, growing more concerned. "I don't suppose you recognize either of us, then?" Phainon shakes his head regretfully. "Do you remember where you are? Or the prophecy, your role in it?"

Phainon… doesn't remember much at all. Just a jumbled mess of vague feelings about things. And those are difficult to navigate as it is without the full knowledge of, well, anything.

"Sorry," he says again, regretful. "Not even my family."

She stiffens, but waves the unnecessary apology off, already busying herself with examining his head again. She gently angles it so that she can have a clear view of the back, where the injury must be. And in the process, she directs his face directly toward Mydei. Phainon can feel some warmth where her fingers are touching, and is rather sure another stream of light is coming from them.

"I would advise against jumping in front of me in such a manner again," Mydei breaks the silence, seemingly off-handed. His intense gaze tells another story. "You might find yourself with a broken arm instead, because I won't let you."

Phainon rolls his eyes, a bout of annoyance spiking up. "I'm sorry, would you rather be the one without your memories?" He snarks back without a thought spared. "I might not remember you, but clearly we are boyfriends or something of the sort. In what world would I prefer you getting hurt?"

Another person makes a noise somewhere at the back of the room, and Phainon looks over Mydei's shoulder to see another girl sitting on a chair in the corner. He wonders briefly why she hasn't made her way over yet, but doesn't think much of it.

She has pale lilac hair, pointy ears peeking out of the strands. Phainon glances over her dress, a white fabric shaped to resemble bandages and bones. Multiple butterflies adorn it, alongside impressive detailing. Her skin is of a concerningly light shade, almost ashy. Phainon wonders if she's another patient.

"Oh. Hello," he greets her with a bright smile.

She hesitantly waves at him, eyes jumping from him to Mydei.

"Boyfriends," Mydei repeats in a strange tone. Almost like he's never uttered the word before.

That throws Phainon for a loop. Are they not? What else would those intense emotions inside of him be, or the odd protective concern Mydei directs at him? Phainon is rather sure there is no way he wouldn't be attracted to the man before him. Lost memories or not. And why wouldn't he try to make a move if he has feelings and is attracted to him? He doesn't remember anything, but he knows he can be persistent and quite convincing when he wants to.

Of course they must be boyfriends.

"The kind doctor just said you waited at my bedside this entire time," he points out readily. "Why would you do that if we weren't in a relationship?"

The man blinks at him, dumbfounded. "I— Your logic astounds me," he gets out eventually, a little strangled. "Castorice is also here. Will you claim you are in a relationship with her as well?"

Castorice. Must be the girl sitting so far away. Phainon glances at her again and opens his mouth to say something.

She beats him to it. "You know very well I only visited him for an hour or two a day, Lord Mydei," she says pleasantly. Her eyes crinkle a little when she smiles. "Unlike you, who spent nights and days here, refusing to listen when urged to take some rest."

Phainon points at her, feeling his point has been proved for him. He stares expectantly at Mydei, who in turn stubbornly stares at the ceiling.

"No sign of permanent brain damage," the healer lady then says. A smile shines through her tone alone. She retreats, and Phainon can rotate his head again, stop staring. He doesn't. "This should wear off within a few days."

Phainon is more interested in watching Mydei. Despite all his aggravating comments and denials, his shoulders lower in clear relief, and the scowl loses some of its intensity. Phainon is sure everyone in the room was worried for him, but Mydei's reaction feels different.

He hums, narrows his eyes at the man. "Are you sure we aren't in a relationship?"

"I don't believe you," Phainon announces when he's done eating, empty plates put away on the bedside table. It was a delicious meal; Phainon will have to ask later who made it. They have the potential to be an outstanding chef.

"What is it now?" Mydei asks, and Phainon gets an impression he is stifling a sigh. Or a groan.

Phainon isn't deterred by the lack of enthusiasm. "We must be in a relationship," he tells him with all the conviction he can muster.

"I believe the subject has been discussed already," Mydei says, leaning back in his seat. "Two people confirmed that we are not, in fact, in a relationship."

"We could have kept it a secret from them," Phainon reasons. It's not unlikely.

"And why would we ever do that," Mydei asks, but he says it so flatly it's more of a statement.

Phainon shrugs. "How would I know? I don't have my memories."

"As insufferable as ever, HKS." Phainon's brows furrow a little at the foreign word. "Alright. Let's hear it, then. What is it that has you convinced of this?"

"You don't seem like someone who is easily moved, but you were openly concerned about my well-being." Not that he assumes Mydei is uncaring. But from his interactions with the other two, Phainon gathered that he tends to be more stoic in his interactions with others. "You are still a little tense, and I'm starting to think it will remain that way until I'm out of this bed or even until I regain my memories."

Phainon may be placing too much hope on his importance here; Mydei may have other worries plaguing his mind. But for whatever reason, deep down he knows it's unusual for him to display his concern about anything. So he will hold onto this, even if he may sound delusional.

"You continuously stop me from fiddling with the bandages even though the wound is healed enough that it wouldn't disturb it," he continues after a short pause. "You brought me food, probably from some restaurant, because it tastes better than what they have in the infirmary. So, you take care of me. And even when I'm being annoying on purpose, you are kind of exasperated, but you freely indulge me."

And there's a certain look in his eyes that wasn't there when he regarded the two girls, but Phainon cannot bring himself to say it. It feels a little fragile, even if he wants to dig deep, scratch at it like a scab until it's torn off and reveals the raw shape beneath it.

They could be best friends, he supposes. The label is confusing, though, prompting a strong surge of pride at the prospect, but also despair. He likes it, but not entirely.

Mydei studies him for a brief moment, but Phainon doesn't waver. He is sure of this. Eventually, Mydei shakes his head, corners of his lips ticking up just the slightest amount. "Even if those don't necessarily point to us being in a relationship, you are infuriatingly perceptive when you want to be."

"I am glad you acknowledge my observations," Phainon says, letting his lips stretch into a grin rather than a tiny smile like his companion's. "Well, what are we, then? There's no one else here, so you can tell me. Boyfriends? Or do we not like the term, so it's partners? It does sound better. No way, husbands? But I don't see a—"

A hand clasps over his mouth with astonishing speed. It wasn't exactly needed, because at the same time, Phainon looks up and sees pink dusting Mydei's ears and cheekbones, his scowl returning but with an embarrassed tinge to it, and that's enough to have Phainon trailing off. Forgetting where he was taking that sentence to begin with.

There are more important matters. Such as the fact that Mydei appears to be flustered.

Titans, Phainon refuses to believe he wasn't in love with this man before today.

"Stop getting ahead of yourself," Mydei hisses at him, lacking his usual composure. At what, an insinuation they might be husbands?

Phainon stares, transfixed. Yeah. Yeah, flustering him might be the best thing ever. Maybe they are together and haven't spoken about marriage yet?

He grabs the offending hand and drags it away from his face, resisting the urge to lace their fingers together and see what reaction that might provoke.

"Fine," he concedes. He isn't about to give up as a whole, but for now, he will give it a rest. Still, might as well try asking outright, "What are we, then?"

Mydei glances away, letting out a hum as if that's an acceptable answer.

Phainon rolls his eyes. What else is he supposed to assume the nature of their relationship is when Mydei refuses to reveal it himself? Realistically, there is only one conclusion he can come to.

 ࣪˖ ☽ ✴ ☾ ˖  ࣪

Once Phainon is let out of the bed, Mydei leads him to his quarters before leaving him to his own devices. Phainon isn't sure whether abandoning a person without any memories is responsible, but he gets an impression Mydei would have stayed for a bit longer if he had asked.

He doesn't ask. In fact, it's a great opportunity to find out more on his own.

Maybe Mydei hoped he would embarrass himself in front of people if he was left without supervision, a form of payback for being so stubbornly insistent about the undefined nature of their relationship. That might come later.

Phainon snoops through his own rooms, noting with interest various antiques and relics littering most surfaces. Some weapons are carefully propped up against the wall, the bed left in a state between unmade and haphazardly tidied up. There isn't… much, in all honesty. It's more of a storage room than anything else.

Nothing overly personal, and nothing that could point to his past. No photos, no journals, no letters, no knick-knacks that could paint a picture of his childhood interests. It's not so disappointing; he isn't particularly interested in what led him to this point in life. He would rather know what's going on in the present.

Determined, he takes a quick stroll through the Kephale Plaza. His main objectives are the smithy and the store with antiques, as those seem to be his primary interests, but he takes the time to stop and chat with other locals as well. Puts on a smile and lets them lead the conversation, nods encouragingly, and offers non-answers to questions, directing them back to whatever thread of conversation offered the most interesting information.

It's easy.

People trust and like him, gushing about the gossip and expressing their concerns. They don't even find it too strange when he asks what turns out to be very obvious questions, content to chat with him. He chuckles and mentions humble beginnings, gains the name of a village, Aedes Elysiae. It fills him with sorrow, and Phainon doesn't have to search far to understand he won't find anyone of the same origins in this city-state.

By the end of the day, he finds out the names of his comrades and their functions. Where they come from and what their standing in Okhema is.

Phainon is a Chrysos Heir, apparently. Bound by fate, a beacon of hope for the civilians. He cuts his pinky later just to check. A drop of ichor wells up to the surface, confirming it. He feels strangely empty about the fact.

The girls from before, Castorice and Hyacine, are also Chrysos Heirs. So is the apparent leader of Okhema, though she is busy enough that he doesn't expect to meet her before the effects of his injury fade.

And Mydei is one too, which he might as well have guessed on his own from the way he carries himself. What does catch him off guard is that he is a prince.

 ࣪˖ ☽ ✴ ☾ ˖  ࣪

"Am I supposed to call you by Your Highness?" Phainon drops down to sit at the edge of a building, nudging his shoulder against Mydei's. He thinks they might be regularly meeting here. He's not sure how he would've stumbled onto this random rooftop otherwise.

Mydei throws him a sidelong glance before refocusing on the view stretching out in front of them. It's a great view. High monuments of rocks decorated with greenery, rainbows weaving around them, clouds drifting through the air, and the imposing statue of the Titan. Phainon isn't really interested.

"Hmph," Mydei breathes out, a gentle noise rather than a sign of real irritation. "When have you ever done what you are supposed to do?"

"Smart," Phainon snorts, smiling despite himself. "Insulting me when I don't have the memories to call on and defend myself."

Mydei turns his head to actually look at him, smiles softly in slight amusement and fondness. His eyes swim with both of those emotions, pupils not exactly the angry pin needles they were when Phainon got on his nerves. Slightly larger, hiding a little bit of his irises.

Phainon cannot remember what exactly his favorite color is. It doesn't come to him, and when he tries to stare at various shades, only a vague appreciation for multiple ones appears. But he looks at Mydei and feels nostalgic when his eyes fall on the pale blond hair, feels longing when he stares into the bright gold gaze that bores into him.

And the vibrant red that he cannot put his finger on. The color of his markings, but also of various clothing garments, which he seems to own. He doesn't know what it is that he feels in reaction to it, but he certainly appreciates the visual sharp contrast it creates. It suits Mydei so well.

Phainon struggles to take in all the details of his appearance. It's too much. The messy hair with one single braid, the slightly bumpy nose, and the red marks underlining one of his eyes. Lips stretched into an attractive smirk, and he thinks he saw some sharp canines earlier.

He inhales, and he's half certain his admiration must be showing on his face as he continues staring.

"What," Mydei prompts him eventually, already exasperated.

"Your beauty is distracting," he breathes out. His own voice comes out incredibly soft, softer than he intended to. He clears his throat and tries for a more flirtatious and humorous tone. "You must be aware of it. But have I ever told you that you are overwhelmingly beautiful?"

Mydei doesn't turn away as he expected him to. Sadly, he doesn't get flustered this time around either. One of his brows rises, and he appears more indulgent than anything else.

"Deliverer," he huffs with amusement. "You once entered my name into a beauty contest."

"I did?" Now, that's surprising. He was forward with his attraction to Mydei, at the very least. Where did he fail, then? If he failed. "Huh. That's unfair to other contestants. How were they supposed to compete?"

Mydei snorts and looks away from him. He brings one of his knees up and rests his elbow against it, glancing at the large form of Kephale. "Shouldn't you be more concerned with your missing memories than this foolishness?"

Phainon doesn't take the bait, though it's tempting. "They are meant to return sooner or later, it doesn't matter," he waves Mydei off. Why worry about something that he can do nothing about? He would rather fix what his past self never managed. And, just to annoy Mydei a little bit more, Phainon returns to his favorite subject as of late. "Is it because I am common-born? Can you only marry a princess of a foreign nation to strengthen the political relations?"

He blinks at him innocently when Mydei glares at him incredulously.

"I think you've been reading too many fantasy books, whether you remember them or not," Mydei comments dryly. A little judgmental. "Kremnoan royalty is under no such obligation. Our partners are chosen by us alone once they are deemed worthy."

That is valuable information. It signifies that all Phainon needs is to prove himself to Mydei, instead of potentially fighting the entire system of traditions and values placed on him as a royal.

"And am I?" He asks before he can think better of it, curiosity sparked. "Worthy."

Mydei's lips part. For a moment, no words come forth. He closes his mouth, swallows as he looks away from Phainon again. "It's of no relevance."

Phainon resists the urge to shove Mydei and have him fall from the roof while he least expects it. He has a feeling it would result in a chase across the market, and as fun as that would have been, this is more important. He can always goad Mydei into something ridiculous once his memory is back. For now, he would rather achieve something that his regular self apparently isn't capable of.

"I will court you," he swears with genuine conviction. "I'm not entirely sure how, but I will show you that I am worthy of your affection."

Mydie hums, unconvinced. "Suit yourself."

 ࣪˖ ☽ ✴ ☾ ˖  ࣪

As it turns out, Mydei's parents are long since dead. The next best thing, a man named Krateros, is out of the question. Phainon doesn't have enough knowledge of Kremnoan history and Mydei's life not to make a fool of himself immediately upon opening his mouth.

He tried approaching Krateros, but he turned on his heel and left the very moment he laid his eyes on him. The man gives an impression that he won't accept anything less than the appropriate Kremnoan traditions, and while Phainon would love nothing more than to deliver, he fears that in his current state, he would only sabotage his own chances.

There is someone who seemed remotely enthusiastic about the idea of him and Mydei together, though.

"Castorice," he calls in a greeting, jogging over when he spots her near the Hall of Respite. She stands in the gazebo, far away from other people. The music played by the organist fills the space. "Hi."

"Hello, Lord Phainon." She smiles, taking a step back when he nears her. Oh, right. That thing where she harms people if they get too close to her. Phainon stops, rubbing the back of his head awkwardly. He forgot about it. Again, because he just talked to someone about it. "How are you feeling?" She asks pleasantly.

"I'm doing fine. Not even thinking about the lost memories and all," he waves her question off with a chuckle. "A matter more important occupies my mind. I would appreciate some help, but I'll be grateful if we could just talk about it."

Castorice's smile widens before she nods eagerly. Phainon feels warm at her readiness to help, the kindness she looks at him with. Just as he is sure there is something more between him and Mydei, he knows Castorice is his friend.

And she happens to be very excited to discuss his relationship with Mydei.

 ࣪˖ ☽ ✴☾ ˖  ࣪

"Have we really fought for ten days and nights on our first meeting?" Phainon asks right as he saddles up to Mydei, having ensured he approached as quietly as possible.

Mydei doesn't even flinch, frowning as he inspects a book displayed in one of the stands. Phainon pouts, and Mydei sighs. "I was foolish to fall under the illusion that you may leave me alone for a few days due to the circumstances, wasn't I?"

"Yeah, you were," Phainon agrees readily, biting on his tongue so that he doesn't stick it out when Mydei glares at him. "Why would I leave you alone? I explicitly told you I would court you. Even if it's pointless since we are already together."

A woman nearby gasps, wide eyes jumping between the two of them in a manner similar to Castorice when he first called them boyfriends. Brimming with excitement and curiosity. It's still odd how invested people appear to be in their lives.

"Great," Mydei says under his breath, shoulders tensing. He abandons the book and starts walking away without a word, forcing Phainon to jog in order to catch up.

Phainon glances back at the woman, sees her clutch at another's elbow and talk to her excitedly. Oh.

"They—" He turns his gaze back to Mydei, but words die on his tongue. He's already fucked up, hasn't he? Titans. Maybe that's why they aren't together. "I'm sorry. You are famous among people. I didn't think of what their reaction might be upon hearing that."

"Infamous would be more fitting. You are the golden boy, Deliverer," Mydei says, somewhat resigned. He runs one hand through his hair. "Don't concern yourself with it. I will have to pay a visit to Verax Leo later, and that's it. This is a recurring subject among the people."

Phainon hums, but doesn't respond otherwise, subdued. He isn't one to give up so easily, but the fact that he managed to do something wrong this quickly isn't very encouraging. There must be a reason why Mydei is so reluctant to even entertain the idea of being in a relationship. Or admit to it.

"That battle we got into upon our first meeting," Mydei speaks up once they are far enough from the people, walking side by side. "It was your fault."

Phainon almost cringes. Not only did he cause an inconvenience with the impending rise of rumors, but now he brought up what must have been a very stupid first impression he made. Great going.

Twice now, actually. He also stupidly choked on water when he first caught a glimpse of Mydei after waking up.

Except Mydei is back to being more relaxed now that they are alone with no one else to overhear them, and he has regained some of the fondness as he regards Phainon. Their fight is not a bad memory for him, then. That's a relief.

It serves him to regain some of his confidence, and he remembers how he planned the conversation to go. He asks with all the cheekiness he can muster. "Isn't that a courting ritual in your culture already?" Or at least it matches the other story Castorice told him. About his parents. "We've been dating since that day, haven't we?"

He isn't so confident in that theory anymore, but he refuses to back down. He thinks anyone else would've lost their patience with him by now, told him to shut up already about the non-existent relationship. But Mydei only makes a thoughtful noise, calm as ever. By Kephale, he—

"You goaded me into that fight, obnoxiously so. You have a talent for affecting my better judgment. I ended up telling my army to stand down, and they witnessed us fight for ten days and ten nights." He hesitates momentarily before adding, "If we were to follow in my parents' steps, we would've gotten engaged immediately, yes."

"We should have," Phainon comments petulantly under his breath, and is rewarded by a short laugh spilling from Mydei's lips. Phainon's stomach jumps.

"I was furious with you," Mydei reminisces, staring at the landscape as they continue walking. Phainon stares at his side profile. It's becoming s a pattern. "You dragged me into that unnecessary fight—as enjoyable as it turned out to be—and then you had the gall to call a draw before either of us could claim victory." He meets Phainon's gaze with fondness. "As infuriating as I found you back then, you did gain my respect for keeping up with me."

Not that bad of a first impression, then. Phainon hums in consideration, kicking a nearby rock. "Is the bar for keeping up with you really that high?"

Mydei shows him a sharp smirk, eyes gaining a slightly feral glint. A shiver travels up Phainon's spine, and he is filled with an urge to witness Mydei in his element.

"I can grind entire armies to the ground," he says in a matter-of-fact manner. "Not quite with a singular strike like Nikador, but I am the strongest fighter Okhema has to offer."

Phainon blinks at that, not having expected a competence quite that high. People's accounts of him varied, mostly under the guise of prejudice from Okhemans and favoritism by Kremnoans. Could Mydei be messing with him? Is it humanly possible to be that strong? And, most importantly, "And I can keep up?"

He hasn't tried fighting yet, but he might soon if that's the case. He is curious how good he might be. It's one thing to enjoy a battle; it's another to be good at it. He imagined himself to be perhaps slightly above average.

Phainon scoffs, and his hand twitches to shove at Mydei. "You would still lose even if I were going easy on you."

 ࣪˖ ☽ ✴ ☾ ˖  ࣪

Crouching down, Phainon pokes at Mydei's cheek. It's childish, and he would have thought it would be at the very least effective, but there is no reaction. And here he was fully prepared to jump back at the first sign of retaliation. He pokes again, and still nothing.

A man like Mydei doesn't wake up at the slightest movement? Odd.

Phainon shifts slightly, brushing the messy bangs out of Mydei's eyes. As unfairly pretty as ever. Mildly annoyed with the flawless picture Mydei makes—not even drooling in his sleep like normal people do—Phainon takes a strand of hair and yanks on it.

Not harshly, because he values his life.

Fingers wrap around his wrist painfully hard and frighteningly fast. There isn't a single trace of sleep in Mydei's features, overcome with fierce focus that might be reserved for his enemies. Phainon immediately plasters on a winning smile and waves with what little movement he has in his hand.

"We are going to the baths," he announces.

Mydei slowly relaxes until he slumps back into the pillows, sighing softly as he drops the hold on Phainon's wrist. Thank Titans for that. Phainon subtly rubs feeling back into it.

"You barged into my quarters," Mydei observes, speaking through a yawn. A rare and rather undignified image that Phainon deeply enjoys.

"Your door was unlocked," Phainon points out.

"That's not an invitation."

"The fact I didn't lose a limb for it is invitation enough," Phainon jokes, enjoying the tired stare he gets in return.

"It's remarkable how you retain your insufferable personality despite the memory loss." Mydei runs one hand through his hair, and it falls into its usual patterns. "You are more carefree and less restrained, but still so undeniably you that it's easy to forget."

Phainon lowers himself fully to the ground, crossing his legs. He hums lightly. "Does it mean I'm always this obsessed?"

Mydei regards him with dry amusement. "At least you are self-aware."

"Can you blame me?" Phainon leans forward, resting one elbow against the furniture. "You are perfect—" Mydei snorts derisively at that, and Phainon continues before a cutting remark can follow. "Shut up. You are the most skilled fighter Amphoreus has to offer. You know me in and out, and you can handle me even when I'm being an idiot, or a mess, or just plain annoying.

"You portray that image of a regal, scathing, prideful royal on the surface, but you care so much, don't you?" Phainon smirks a little when Mydei's lips press into a thin line. "I caught you playing with the kids, and I know you have frequent meetings with the officials to ensure the peace between Okhema and Kremnos. You cook for the Chrysos Heirs, know all their favorite meals by heart, and it's always delicious. Have I mentioned you are beautiful? I have a hard time imagining a man more attractive than you."

Phainon chuckles a little to himself, feeling giddy with the discussion. If he didn't love Mydei before, he doesn't think he would be capable of stopping now. He doubts it, though. He doesn't think it's possible to develop feelings so intense this quickly without a strong foundation. They must have been there already. Dormant, in the worst-case scenario. Or ignored, as is most likely.

"And, you know," Phainon says conversationally, meeting Mydei's eyes with delight. He loves those eyes so much. "I think you love me too. Because the way you look at me, it's like I am…" Valuable. Worthy. The best thing that could have happened. "The same way I imagine I look at you," he finishes lamely, smile crooked.

A hand smashes into his face, fingers splayed wide across his eyes and cheeks, and Phainon laughs. Loud and open, eyes crinkling as he looks through the gaps and glimpses the bright flush on Mydei's cheeks. It suits him so well. He wants to kiss him across the reddened skin, embarrass him more, and fluster him to no end.

"I think I courted you sufficiently," he mumbles, prying the hand off his face. Red lines wrap around it artfully, just like the rest of his body. He cannot resist pressing a kiss against the knuckles, a barely-there press of lips. It's so worth it when Mydei snatches his hand back as if burned.

"Did you."

Phainon nods, undeterred by the flattest tone he's heard from Mydei yet. The intended effect of supposed irritation is ruined by the pupils dilating just so and the pink color adorning his ears. Phainon wondered when he would manage to evoke this reaction again.

"I got you a gift," Phainon counts out on his fingers. "Two, in fact. Gems out of my own collection, which are a meaningful offering. Then, a brand new set of custom gauntlets made out of the best materials. I baked for you—"

"I recall it going a little differently," Mydei cuts in, apparently having regained some of his composure to poke fun at Phainon. "Feels like I baked for myself, actually."

"I baked for you," Phanion repeats stubbornly. "And it was a delicious cake. I am currently making sure you can unwind at the end of a long day by taking you to the baths—we are still going, if you were wondering. We conversed a lot. We spared, twice, which is one of your favorite pastimes."

He waves his fingers in the air, six of them straightened out. Mydei glances at them and then raises an eyebrow at Phainon. Phainon only stares back expectantly.

"And?" Mydei prompts eventually.

"And I think we should be going out," Phainon sums up for him with a sunny grin.

Mydei glances at the ceiling as if asking the Titans for strength. "And what, pray tell, do I do when you regain your memories and decide you no longer want this?"

"Beat me up for being an idiot who is actively sabotaging not only mine but also your happiness," Phainon replies without missing a beat. Honestly, he would beat himself up if he could. He desperately hopes he is not that much of a coward to pass up on all the foundation he laid out in the last few days.

"I don't need your permission to beat you up," Mydei says, probably just to be contrary.

"Great. I'm glad that's settled." Phainon gets to his feet, stretching out his spine and wincing at the crack it produces. "Now we can go to the baths."

Mydei blinks at him once and then promptly turns onto his side, pretending to fall back asleep with his back to Phainon. "Just leave me to my sleep, Deliverer."

Phainon snorts softly. "You will sleep better after you relax with me," he promises.

Then, he forcibly drags him up to his feet, grinning when Mydei pretends to be annoyed about it. His eyes betray him. Fond. Always so fond.

 ࣪˖ ☽ ✴ ☾ ˖  ࣪

Fingers tangle into Phainon's hair, and he nearly whines at the soothing sensation. It's precisely what he needed, except maybe some medicine.

"What's wrong?" Mydei asks.

"I have a migraine," Phainon whines, raising his head to direct a hopefully pathetic enough stare at Mydei. He cheers internally when the hand doesn't slip away from his hair.

"Go to Hyacine," Mydei tells him, not very concerned with his misery.

Phainon hums, then smiles brightly. "Was hoping your sparkling personality would soothe it."

He is smacked right on the top of his head.

He lets out a yelp, hand going up to shield himself. "I just told you I have a migraine!"

"You will be fine," Mydei dismisses him, and Phainon makes a mental note to be as inconvenient as possible the next time Mydei is recovering from a death, which never fails to leave him with a headache. Ah. "You will probably regain your memory soon."

"Yeah," Phainon agrees, dropping his hand from where he was massaging the sore spot where Mydei hit him. "I remember my parents now. And Cyrene. Then it gets a little messy, but I've got memories of traveling on my own in the darkness."

He sighs, glancing over at Theodoros arguing about something or other with Kyros in the distance. Phainon was in the middle of shopping when his head started aching, nearly as bad as when he first woke up, and he had to find a secluded place to rest. Not secluded enough.

"I remember people's names, too," he muses when Mydei doesn't say anything. "And small things, though no concrete memories of my time in Okhema. Like the fact that Castorice enjoys writing. You get migraines when you're recovering, and you never let them keep your bandages on for longer than five hours. Professor Anaxa is passionate about the dromas. Lady Aglaea is passionate about sewing fashionable dresses. They are both also very passionate about hating each other."

Mydei snorts at that. "That they are."

They lapse into a comfortable silence, content to just sit together. Phainon likes that. He talks a lot by nature, but it gets tiring sometimes. He is glad that, for once, he doesn't feel the need to fill in the silence.

He tries not to think too much. His migraine has lessened enough to be considered a dull ache at the side of his head with random spikes of pain that pass quickly enough. He's not sure if it would worsen it, but he doesn't want to think about his memories and what he might see in them soon enough. Or maybe it's just his sanity he wishes to preserve.

Still, he swallows and decides to throw caution to the wind. What has he got to lose?

"Can you tell me at least once?" Phainon asks sheepishly. He hopes the desperation he feels cannot be detected in his tone. "Before my memories are back and I potentially revert to being too big a coward to do something about it."

"Why would I?" Mydei asks, an amused smirk curling his lips up. "Aren't I supposed to beat you up in that scenario?"

"Yeah, well." Phainon shrugs, scratching the back of his head. He can feel a small scar at the base of his skull if he presses his fingers hard enough. He doesn't, because it's still painful. "You've been indulging me all this time. Why not once more?"

"Come back and tell me yourself again once you have your memories," Mydei tells him, unrelenting. "And then, you have my word, I will say them without hesitation."

It's not the exact words he wishes him to speak aloud. But the sentiment is all the same, and Phainon's cheeks warm at it. It's the first time Mydei acknowledged it. It's good enough for him. It's good enough if he never actually says those three words, actually, as long as he lets Phainon know he feels the same way. It's enough.

"So mean," Phainon gives a put-upon sigh, turning in his seat and pulling one leg up so that he can fully face Mydei. He wonders if he lets himself admire the man in front of him so openly. Or whether he usually tries to censure those thoughts as soon as they come up. He cannot imagine the effort it must take. "How about a small kiss?" He asks cheekily, expecting immediate refusal.

But Mydei, determined to keep Phainon off-kilter at all times, leans forward. Phainon freezes in place, feels all his muscles lock up. Mydei brushes Phainon's bangs away and presses his lips against his forehead. He lingers for a moment, pulling back only enough to meet Phainon's eyes. He looks a little sad and resigned, but mostly accepting and affectionate. Finding a way to give in to Phainon's request.

Indulgent.

Phainon cannot comprehend how he could seemingly spend so much time with this man, become his best friend, and never go further than that. He prays to Kephale that the incredulity and frustration he feels at his own actions remain vicious enough to burn through whatever stupid reservations he may have held.

"If you wake up to find yourself ashamed of your words and actions these past few days," Mydei says quietly, busying himself with fixing Phainon's hair, "Do not worry. I can carry these feelings to my grave if you so wish. We can go back to how we were right before your injury if you say a single word. I won't hold it against you."

"Mydei, who wouldn't fall in love with you?" Phainon asks as soon as Mydei falls silent, a little breathless.

Mydei runs fingers through his hair again, just like he did when he first found him sitting away from the public, and gets up to leave without another word.

Phainon lets him go because he worries that if he gets a hold of him again, he might not let go.

 ࣪˖ ☽ ✴ ☾ ˖  ࣪

"I think it's cute," Castorice tells him with a small smile that doesn't fool him one bit.

Mydei clicks his tongue. "You thought it was cute when he got drunk that one time and started pestering my soldiers to teach him Kremnoan," he points out with an unimpressed stare. "And then he threw up on one of them, and I had to drag him away to his quarters."

"Lord Phainon has you on his mind at all times, even while heavily intoxicated," Castorice tells him pleasantly, not losing her enthusiasm. "It's endearing."

Mydei says nothing.

It's not like they don't realize they are in love. It's an open secret, the perfect gossip material for the civilians and Chrysos Heirs alike. Will Mydei and Phainon get together this time? He is certain that Cipher is actively running a plethora of bets despite barely ever setting foot in Okhema these days.

Mydei doesn't push things along. Phainon doesn't reach for them either. They are content enough with how things are, perhaps frightened by the possibility of fully letting go just for one of them to die. Not that Mydei would admit it to anyone, and he doesn't think Phainon would either.

And so, it became a waiting game, wondering when things might finally give.

The answer is apparently memory loss. And loss of the self-restraint that comes with it.

"You should take that step for him if he doesn't, Lord Mydei," Castorice breaks the silence. "You could both make each other happy."

They both look over when the large door to the library opens and closes loudly, Phainon's figure emerging.

It takes Mydei only one look to know everything has returned to him. His eyes are haunted in a way he hasn't figured out how to cover just yet, or at least not how to hide it from Mydei. He holds himself in a more collected manner as opposed to the loose stance from the last few days, each step measured.

"I will give you some privacy," Castorice says mirthfully, though Mydei is unsure whether she realizes Phainon regained his memories just yet.

He gives her a nod as she quickly leaves, not taking his eyes off Phainon. It's difficult to tell what his intentions are, but if he is seeking Mydei out already, it cannot be anything bad. Mydei would assume that he would sooner wallow in the privacy of his own rooms at the embarrassment of the last few days than make a scene.

"Welcome back, Phainon," he carefully greets once the man is close enough.

And doesn't get much further than that, not even in his thoughts, when Phainon is finally right in front of him. One hand settles on Mydei's bare shoulder, grip tight and desperate. Mydei gets so far as letting out a questioning noise before lips crush against his painfully, with so much force he has to lean back in his seat. Phainon only presses closer. He licks over Mydei's mouth once, not even waiting for Mydei to part them before he pulls away with a self-satisfied grin.

Dazed, Mydei runs his tongue over his own lips. Hysterically, he realizes it's actually Phainon's spit covering them. What the—

"Hey, Mydei," Phainon calls, not even looking as he hooks an ankle around a nearby chair's leg and pulls it close. He sits down, so close that their knees are touching. He doesn't look away from Mydei, transfixed. And his eyes are bright and open, so similar to how he looked at Mydei not so long ago. "I fell in love with you when you ruined my favorite coat for the first time, mocked me about it for an hour straight afterward, and then punched me in the face on the way to Okhema so hard that my nose broke in two places."

Mydei clenches his fingers on empty air, and he can do nothing much but blink at Phainon. Whatever he may have expected, it wasn't anything this intense. Phainon's grin is blinding. Cheerful and relieved. It has Mydei wondering who would ever need the Dawn Device when Phainon can smile like this. He's never seen him so delighted. He would indulge him in anything until his last breath if it meant he remained so genuinely happy.

"And I thought," Phainon continues, knocking his knee against Mydei's once. "I thought you were the most insufferable and stuck-up guy ever. And I thought you were perfect."

And Mydei, Mydei remembers the pleasant ache in his bones after their fight, the intense satisfaction of a good spar, and the disappointment at leaving it unresolved. Remembers Phainon breaking his forearm after he broke his nose, and pointedly snapping the bone back into place without a care. Watching the blue eyes darken at the nonchalance of it, sneering back with something. He remembers watching Phainon interact with his soldiers on the way back, laughing with them and fitting in against all odds.

Insufferable, just as he called Mydei, and tempting beyond belief.

"How would you feel about setting that indigo steel into a ring, after all?" He asks, quieter and softer. Mydei hasn't responded yet, but Phainon doesn't lose his confidence. He waits patiently as if to say, Your turn.

Mydei lets himself sit and take the sight in front of him for one more beat before he sends Phainon a sharp grin. With no warning, he grabs him by the leather strap on his chest and yanks him closer again. Phainon yelps as he nearly falls out of his chair, clumsily stabilizing himself with one hand on the table and the other on Mydei's knee.

Endearing.

"I love you," Mydei says against Phainon's lips, feeling the smile they stretch into.
